title: Deeper/broader R2013+ modeler flag-to-carrier emission invariant
mode: primary-source web research and read-only plan refinement
scope: Trace the R2013+ has_ds_data bit and SAB payload through open-source writer and reader paths
Compare peer conventions with ODA's normative bit meaning and refine the exact supported-profile boundary
Refine existing per-handle AcDs replay/readback acceptance without adding peer execution to the fast loop

method.kind: Current official repository, release-index, and source-documentation review; local plan cross-check
method.limitations: ACadRust docs.rs latest source is mutable and was not bound to the listed 0.6.4 release; its latest AcisData API page still identifies version 0.5.4. ACadSharp PR #1240 is open and undeployed. Peer source patterns are not normative DWG evidence or runtime results.

sources.project: Open Design Alliance Open Design Specification v5.4.1
sources.revision: Official ODA-hosted PDF reviewed 2026-10-18; §§20.4.1 and 24 (printed pp. 106-107 and 244-245)
sources.observed: Section 20.4.1 defines the R2013+ Has DS binary data bit as indicating associated binary data in the data store; section 24 describes AcDb:AcDsPrototype_1b as an ACIS data section with segment/index lookup structures. The specification does not define a universal per-modeler eligibility rule, one-to-one record-key mapping, or solid-semantic guarantee from the bit.

sources.revision: Mutable docs.rs latest source and API reviewed 2026-10-18; release index lists 0.6.4
sources.observed: The writer source derives pending has_ds_data from AcDs route eligibility and contributes_sab before emitting the entity preamble, then queues a SAB entry paired to the entity handle. The reader source distinguishes indexed handle attachment from order fallback. The API/source snapshot is not proven to match the listed release.
PR #1240 remains open and undeployed, depends on the ACDS schema refactor #1174, and its visible writer commit describes ModelerGeometry serialization and unsupported-binary warnings.

sources.revision: Current NEWS and issue status reviewed 2026-10-18; issue report names 0.14.8593
sources.observed: NEWS includes an inline SAT final-block fix. Open issue #1411 reports AcDs/SAB carrier loss on its specifically named 0.14.8593 route. The release note and issue concern different routes and do not establish current behavior.

sources.revision: Read-only audit of the shared worktree source state at HEAD de27a3391a624aba03ca71f3583c4b3a6e6396a9
sources.observed: The common entity encoder emits the bit from hasDsData. The inspected writer stages AcDs payload metadata only for preserved raw modeler-frame replay and validates it against a replayed raw AcDs section; this path is not a general typed modeler DWG serializer.

assessment.planImpact: Refines existing PAR-07/S2/S3/S8 acceptance by separating ODA's coarse bit meaning from the stricter local raw-replay policy. The bidirectional per-handle flag/payload invariant applies only to the admitted AC1027+ REGION/3DSOLID AcDs replay profile; it is not a universal modeler rule or general typed-DWG-authoring claim. No implementation queue or validation cadence change.

implementationReadyChecks: For the admitted AC1027+ REGION/3DSOLID AcDs raw-replay profile, assert that the external-data bit and exact linked payload agree both ways for each entity handle and owner path; do not generalize to BODY or other data-store object types.
Exercise empty, supported, and refused modeler-data cases plus distinct two-body payloads under object-order/handle-order permutation using locally generated in-memory or scratch-only material.

Inspect the physical wire bit, AcDs key/framing/hash, and output disposition separately; count the local path as same-version raw replay, not general typed AcDs authoring or independent semantic proof.
Keep AC1024-and-earlier inline modeler serialization as a separate profile; use ODA and producer traces for wire authority.
Use only the owning focused build, selector, and existing CTest for a later implementation slice; do not add external fixtures, dependencies, peer-per-slice runs, or full-suite runs.
